title: A browser creature collector built with generative AI
author: Old-Initiative6499
selftext: Alderwick is a browser-based creature collector with a semi AFK trap and return loop and generative AI was part of its development. Where it helped most was the repetitive work pressure testing trap timing and catch-rate balance, boilerplate like state persistence and timer logic, and first draft flavour text that was then rewritten heavily. What it couldn't do was define the game: the creature roster and the forest's get stranger the deeper you go, identity had to come from the developer, because AI-generated concepts were generic and mostly discarded. Pacing was the same whether the first session feels like a slow burn or just slow is a judgment call AI can't make. The recurring lesson seems to be that AI output needs review. AI compressed the parts that don't define the game and left the interesting 40% untouched.

comments.author: thecrownforge
comments.body: The first trap timer seems like the key test for this loop. Do people come back to see what they caught, or leave before the first result? I'd watch a few new players without explaining the wait, then check how many return. That might tell you whether the first session feels like a slow burn or just slow.
